q: The Bureau of Indian Standards, the national standards body of India, functions under the:
options: Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986
Indian Standards Act, 1947
Weights and Measures Act, 1950
Trade Marks Act, 1999
explanation: The Bureau of Indian Standards is the national standards body of India and it works under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986, which replaced the Indian Standards Act of 1947 and took effect on 1 April 1987.

q: A 'Special Mention' in the Parliament of India refers to:
options: A discussion on a matter of urgent public importance following a statement in the House
A motion for the removal of the Speaker
A motion of no confidence against the Council of Ministers
A matter of sufficient public importance that is raised outside the normal agenda of the House and is not answered
explanation: A Special Mention is a matter of sufficient public importance that a member raises outside the normal agenda of the House and that the Speaker permits to be made, but it is not answered in the House.

q: The 'Question Hour' in the Lok Sabha is the time allotted for:
options: The discussion on the Budget and the Finance Bill
The asking of questions and the answering of them by the ministers
The motions of thanks and the no-confidence motions
The introduction of the private members' bills
explanation: The Question Hour is the first hour of every sitting of the Lok Sabha in which the members ask questions and the ministers answer them on the floor of the House. Starred questions are answered orally, while unstarred ones are answered on the same day in writing.

q: Under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, the notification of a terrorist organisation is issued by:
options: The State Government on the recommendation of the State Police
The Central Government after consultation with the State Government
The Central Bureau of Investigation on its own motion
The National Investigation Agency
explanation: Under Section 35 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, the Central Government notifies an organisation as a terrorist organisation after consultation with the State Government, and the organisation may appeal to the newly created Terrorism Appeal Tribunal.

q: Section 124A of the Indian Penal Code deals with:
options: The offence of being a member of an unlawful organization
The punishment for the murder of a public servant
Sedition, that is the act of bringing or attempting to bring disaffection towards the Government established by law in India
The unlawful assembly of more than twenty persons
explanation: Section 124A of the Indian Penal Code punishes sedition, that is the act of bringing or attempting to bring disaffection towards the Government established by law in India, and the Court of Session tries the offence under the law.

q: The Foreigners Act, 1946 provides for the detention of a foreigner in the interest of:
options: The sovereignty, security and the friendly relations of India
The prevention of the illegal migration of the labour
The enforcement of the foreign exchange regulations
The economic interests of the State
explanation: Section 3 of the Foreigners Act, 1946 empowers the Central Government to detain a foreigner, or to direct that a foreigner be detained, in the interest of the sovereignty, security and the friendly relations of India.

q: The proclamation of a National Emergency under Article 352 can be issued by the President:
options: On the advice of the Chief Minister of the state concerned
On the recommendation of the Lok Sabha alone
On the recommendation of the Election Commission
On the advice of the Union Cabinet
explanation: Article 352 allows the President to proclaim a National Emergency on the advice of the Union Cabinet when the security of India or any part of it is threatened by war, external aggression or armed rebellion. The proclamation must be approved by both Houses within one month by a special majority.

q: The North-Eastern Council was set up under the:
options: Sixth Schedule of the Constitution
North-Eastern Council Act, 1971
North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971
States Reorganisation Act, 1956
explanation: The North-Eastern Council was set up under the North-Eastern Council Act, 1971 to promote the cooperative action and the coordinated development of the north-eastern region. It is not a constitutional body and the Sixth Schedule deals with the administration of the tribal areas.

q: The Unique Identification Authority of India became a statutory body under the:
options: Aadhaar (Unique Identification Authority of India) Act, 2009
Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
Information Technology Act, 2000
Passport (Entry into India) Act, 1920
explanation: The Aadhaar (Unique Identification Authority of India) Act, 2009, later renamed as the Unique Identification Authority of India Act, 2016, made the UIDAI a statutory body, replacing the earlier set up of the Authority as an executive body of the Government of India.

q: A censure motion can be moved in the Lok Sabha against:
options: The Comptroller and Auditor General
The Speaker of the House
A minister
The Deputy Speaker
explanation: A censure motion can be moved against a minister and it is used to express the disapproval of the policies and the conduct of a minister. A motion of no confidence can be moved against the Council of Ministers as a whole.

q: An ordinance can be promulgated by the President only when:
options: The Parliament has been dissolved
The Lok Sabha has adjourned sine die
The Council of States has not passed the Bill
Both the Houses of Parliament are not in session
explanation: Under Article 123, the President can promulgate an ordinance only when either House of Parliament is not in session, and every ordinance must be laid before Parliament and ceases to operate six weeks after Parliament reassembles, unless approved earlier.
